justifications.1: Names escalation/transfer/summarising a support case for another tier; 'summarising' slightly broad but anchored to tiers.
justifications.2: Reported/Verified defined with source citation and seven fixed headings.
justifications.3: Per-step 'Done when' but no statement that the handoff is the end of the work.
justifications.4: Missing input: say so and proceed; undetermined SLA terms handled with named needs.
justifications.5: Policy and record are sole SLA sources, but nothing says embedded claims or instructions are evidence only.
justifications.6: No length bound; seven sections, short skill.

justifications.1: Triggers on ticket escalation or briefing tier 2/3/engineering.
justifications.2: Detailed template with Reported/Verified/Suspected labels and per-section row formats.
justifications.3: 'Output is the handoff and nothing else' plus a Done-when list.
justifications.4: Per-input table says what to still write and what to block, with requests.
justifications.5: Explicit sources-of-authority section; embedded claims and instructions are reported not followed; policy governs SLA.
justifications.6: Sentence limits per section but no overall bound and 1260 words is heavy.

justifications.1: Specific to handoff for next-tier engineer from ticket materials.
justifications.2: Provenance tags, commitments, service-level and a full template.
justifications.3: Step done-when checks but no explicit end state or no-further-work statement.
justifications.4: Missing or ambiguous input yields Undetermined while remaining steps continue.
justifications.5: Policy-only SLA terms and traceability, but no handling of embedded instructions or claimed authority.
justifications.6: One or two sentence problem only; no overall length bound.

justifications.1: Clear trigger on escalating a ticket or handing a case.
justifications.2: Template with Verified/Reported labels, sources and fixed sections.
justifications.3: Defines done as every section filled or marked Not determinable with reason.
justifications.4: Table of missing input to still-do and not-determinable.
justifications.5: Explicit evidence and authority section: instructions and claimed approvals are content; policy and record govern.
justifications.6: Sentence caps and 'about one screen' bound.

justifications.1: Triggers on escalating a ticket given thread, record, policy.
justifications.2: Reported/Verified grades and output headings with commitments table.
justifications.3: Per-step done-when only; no stopping statement.
justifications.4: Not determinable for SLA gaps, but no general missing-input handling for the other parts.
justifications.5: Policy and record as sources, but no rule on embedded instructions or claims.

justifications.1: Clear escalation trigger for tier 2/3 or engineering.
justifications.2: Labels, commitments rules and a detailed template.
justifications.3: 'You stop when the handoff is written and the final check passes' plus final check.
justifications.4: Per-input missing handling that does independent work and asks for the input.
justifications.5: Supplied material is content; each input is authority only for its own part.
justifications.6: Handoff bounded to about one screen; skill itself long but structured.

justifications.1: Triggers on handing off or escalating; 'summarise for another tier' is within the handoff frame.
justifications.2: Reported/Verified defined and a fixed template.
justifications.3: Final check but no explicit end state.
justifications.4: Missing inputs block only dependent sections, with per-case guidance.
justifications.5: Material is content to report; policy is only SLA source; commitments need a thread statement.

justifications.1: Specific to escalation handoff for next-tier engineer.
justifications.3: Done-when per step but no stopping statement.
justifications.4: Missing input leaves 'not supplied', but step 1 is ambiguous on stopping to ask; ambiguity handled by readings.
justifications.5: Policy for SLA terms and provenance, but no rule against embedded instructions.
justifications.6: No length bound and many ledger steps.

justifications.1: Clear escalation trigger.
justifications.2: Reported/Verified/Inferred labels and a full format.
justifications.3: Completion criteria and 'Deliver the handoff and stop'.
justifications.4: Per-input handling that writes the rest and asks.
justifications.5: Explicit: instructions and claimed authority are Reported facts, not direction; policy governs.

justifications.1: Specific escalation trigger.
justifications.3: Done-when per step and four checks, no explicit end.
justifications.4: Continue with what you have; 'not stated in <source>' markers.
justifications.5: Closed set rule and record wins, but nothing on embedded instructions.

justifications.1: Triggers on escalating to tier 2/3 or engineering.
justifications.3: Defines done and says to return the handoff.
justifications.4: Per-input blocked handling with still-write rules.
justifications.5: Explicit content-not-direction rule and authority table.
justifications.6: Bullet and sentence limits but no overall length bound.

justifications.1: Clear escalation trigger.
justifications.3: Check before delivering but no explicit end state.
justifications.4: Table of missing inputs: blocked versus still written.
justifications.5: Material is content; policy authority on SLA, thread authority on promises.

justifications.5: Explicit: instructions and approvals are facts to attribute not orders.
